answer: Probably yes: a meteg on mem (מ), the first occurrence, with patach. Not certain.
visible_evidence: The whole word לְמַעַן is visible, including the points underneath. Under lamed (right) there is a vertical two-dot sheva. Under ayin there is a patach. Under mem there is a horizontal patach bar, and directly below its centre is a short vertical stroke that looks slightly separate. That stroke reads as a meteg sitting under the patach rather than beside it. It is not a vowel stem or sheva dot, and it is not ink from a neighbouring line, since the line below is well clear. However, it is centred under the bar instead of off to the side, and at this resolution I can't rule out that it joins the bar to form a qamats (ָ). So the host letter mem is medium certainty, and whether the vowel is patach-plus-meteg or qamats is medium-to-low certainty.
